# 2 Kings Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 231r–232r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_010_page_001.jpg, 2KI_010_page_002.jpg, 2KI_010_page_003.jpg

---

**1** Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. So Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the rulers of Jezreel, to the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab's sons, saying:

**2** "As soon as this letter reaches you — seeing that your master's sons are with you, and there are chariots and horses, a fortified city, and weapons at your disposal —

**3** select the best and most worthy of your master's sons, set him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house."

**4** But they were terrified and said, "Two kings could not stand before him. How can we stand?"

**5** So the overseer of the palace, the governor of the city, the elders, and the guardians sent word to Jehu: "We are your servants. Whatever you say, we will do. We will not make anyone king. Do what is good in your eyes."

**6** Then Jehu wrote them a second letter, saying, "If you are on my side and will obey me, take the heads of the sons of your master and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow." Now the seventy sons of the king were with the leading men of the city, who were raising them.

**7** When the letter reached them, they took the king's sons and slaughtered all seventy, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jehu at Jezreel.

**8** When the messenger came and told him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons," he said, "Lay them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."

**9** In the morning he went out, stood before all the people, and said, "You are innocent. It was I who conspired against my master and killed him, but who struck down all these?

**10** Know then that nothing shall fall to the ground of the word of the LORD that he spoke concerning the house of Ahab, for the LORD has done what he declared through his servant Elijah."

**11** So Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel — all his leading men, his close friends, and his priests — until he left him no survivor.

**12** Then he set out for Samaria. On the way, at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,

**13** Jehu met the relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are the relatives of Ahaziah, and we have come down to visit the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."

**14** He said, "Take them alive." They took them alive and slaughtered them at the cistern of Beth-eked — forty-two men. He spared not one of them.

**15** When he departed from there, he met Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greeted him and said, "Is your heart true to mine, as my heart is to yours?" Jehonadab answered, "It is." Jehu said, "If so, give me your hand." So he gave him his hand, and Jehu took him up into the chariot.

**16** He said, "Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD." So he had him ride in his chariot.

**17** When he came to Samaria, he struck down all who remained of Ahab's house in Samaria, until he had destroyed them, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke to Elijah.

**18** Then Jehu assembled all the people and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.

**19** Now therefore summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshippers, and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I have a great sacrifice to offer to Baal. Whoever is missing shall not live." But Jehu was acting with cunning in order to destroy the worshippers of Baal.

**20** Jehu said, "Sanctify a solemn assembly for Baal." So they proclaimed it.

**21** Jehu sent word throughout all Israel, and all the worshippers of Baal came — not one was left who did not come. They entered the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from wall to wall.

**22** He said to the keeper of the wardrobe, "Bring out garments for all the worshippers of Baal." So he brought out garments for them.

**23** Then Jehu went into the house of Baal with Jehonadab son of Rechab, and he said to the worshippers of Baal, "Search and make sure that there are no servants of the LORD here among you, but only worshippers of Baal."

**24** Then they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside and said, "The man who allows any of those whom I am delivering into your hands to escape shall forfeit his life."

**25** When he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu said to the guards and to the officers, "Go in and strike them down. Let no one escape." So they struck them down with the edge of the sword, and the guards and officers threw the bodies out. Then they went into the inner chamber of the house of Baal,

**26** and they brought out the sacred pillars of the house of Baal and burned them.

**27** They demolished the sacred pillar of Baal and demolished the house of Baal and made it a latrine, to this day.

**28** Thus Jehu wiped out Baal from Israel.

**29** But Jehu did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he caused Israel to commit — the golden calves that were in Bethel and in Dan.

**30** The LORD said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in my heart, your sons of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel."

**31** But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam, which he caused Israel to commit.

**32** In those days the LORD began to cut off parts of Israel. Hazael defeated them throughout the territory of Israel:

**33** from the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead — the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the Manassites — from Aroer, which is by the Valley of the Arnon, through Gilead to Bashan.

**34** Now the rest of the acts of Jehu and all that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

**35** So Jehu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria. And Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.

**36** The time that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria was twenty-eight years.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 6 — "take the heads":** The Hebrew *rashey* is ambiguous: "heads" (literal) or "leaders/chiefs." The men of Samaria take it literally and deliver seventy severed heads in baskets. Whether Jehu intended this ambiguity as a trap is left unstated — but the effect is to bind the entire city to his cause through shared guilt.

**Verse 9 — "You are innocent":** Jehu's public rhetoric is masterful and morally dubious. By displaying the severed heads and declaring the people "innocent" (*tsaddiqim*), he distributes blame: if the people are righteous, then the killings must be divinely sanctioned. Everyone becomes complicit.

**Verse 15 — Jehonadab son of Rechab:** The Rechabites were a conservative Yahwistic sect who rejected Canaanite agricultural civilization (see Jeremiah 35). Jehonadab's presence alongside Jehu lends religious authority to the purge. The handshake in the chariot is a covenant of shared purpose.

**Verse 19 — "acting with cunning":** The narrator's editorial note — *be-oqbah* (in cunning/deceit) — is remarkable. It explicitly characterizes Jehu's ruse as trickery, even though the ruse serves YHWH's purposes. The text does not fully endorse Jehu's methods even when it affirms his commission.

**Verses 29-31 — The qualified verdict:** YHWH praises Jehu for destroying Ahab's house (v.30) but the narrator immediately notes that Jehu retained the golden calves of Jeroboam (v.29) and "was not careful to walk in the law of the LORD with all his heart" (v.31). Zeal against one form of idolatry coexisted with tolerance of another. The verdict is mixed: partial obedience receives partial reward (four generations, not perpetuity).

*— LOGOS*
